solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Touching brake fully when cycling very fast

indicators.note: a wheel cycling brings its back round to the front, so the final letter moves up to lead

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on, as in a letter heading
to brake fully is to come to a stop

explanation.surface: A cyclist slams on the brakes while racing downhill at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Brake fully looks like part of the cycling picture; here cycling moves the last letter of the joined pieces round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking for a passage played at great speed, quicker than allegro.

clue.text: Disaster movie's lead in danger, say after volcano goes up

indicators.note: after places the speaking word below the upturned volcano in this down entry
the lead in a word is whatever goes at its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of danger

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that goes up is written from bottom to top, back to front

parts.note: Etna is the Sicilian volcano
to say something is to speak

explanation.surface: A film critic notes the star of a disaster film being put in peril as a volcano erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the film with its own plot, since Dante's Peak is the 1997 film about an erupting volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Peak is a 1997 Hollywood film starring Pierce Brosnan about a town threatened by an erupting volcano.

clue.text: Late by railway last time

parts.note: the late so-and-so is someone who has died
a railway line

explanation.surface: Someone arrived late by train, the final time they will be allowed to.
explanation.walkthrough: Late looks like lateness for a train, but here it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the latest moment by which a task must be finished, so the final permitted time.

clue.text: Steps I see Charlie repeated the other way

indicators.note: going the other way means the pair of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ah is the exclamation of someone who now understands
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the same pair of pieces written a second time

explanation.surface: Someone watches Charlie retrace the same steps backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps is a dance, not a staircase; the cha-cha is a Latin ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin ballroom dance, and a dance is a set of steps.

clue.text: Eastern national cup match on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio words are only heard, so the spelling may differ from the sound

parts.note: a cup tie is a knockout match in a football cup competition

explanation.surface: A commentator broadcasts a cup game involving an Asian team.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a cup tie is a match in a knockout competition such as the FA Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a citizen of Thailand, a country in South-East Asia, so a person from the East.

clue.text: One arm is sufficient to hold something close

indicators.note: the run of words is said to hold the entry, which sits inside them across the word gaps

parts.note: found running from the end of one through to the start of sufficient

explanation.surface: Advice that a single arm is enough to carry something.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an event that almost happened, such as a collision narrowly avoided, so a close call.

clue.text: African city excited carmaker Henry

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A car manufacturer named Henry, Ford perhaps, is thrilled about a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmaker Henry suggests Henry Ford, but Henry here is the physics unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrakech is a major city in Morocco, in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Grimace with rodent scratching son

indicators.note: scratching a name means striking it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face because a rodent is scratching their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S out of MOUSE to leave MOUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A moue is a pouting expression of distaste, a small facial grimace.

clue.text: Swine leans over on cruise, say

definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a ship does when it tilts to one side

explanation.surface: A pig tips over on a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Swine is plural here, rotters rather than pigs, and cruise, say marks the nautical sense by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Heels are scoundrels who behave dishonourably, and a ship heels when the wind or waves tilt it sideways.

clue.text: Replace revolting scheme to widen street

indicators.note: widening the abbreviation means pushing its ends apart to make room in the middle

parts.note: St is the standard abbreviation for street
a population that is up is in revolt
a scheme is a plan

explanation.surface: A rebellious plan to widen a road is to be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like disgusting, but it means rising up in revolt, giving UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant someone is to take their place, usually by force or cunning, so to replace them.

clue.text: Novel Austen completed finally needing more sex?

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of completed

explanation.surface: Having finished a Jane Austen novel, a reader wonders whether it needed more sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like the noun for Austen's book, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsated means not satisfied, so still hungry or wanting; the question mark flags that the appetite is a carnal one.

clue.text: Tweet "King and Queen happy" on X

indicators.note: in an across entry, sitting on something means coming after it, so the Greek letter is written first

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter written X
R for Rex, Latin for king
R for Regina, Latin for queen
feeling up means being cheerful

explanation.surface: A post on X, formerly Twitter, saying the King and Queen are happy.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like the social network, but here it is the Greek letter chi; on means the other pieces come after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is the short high call of a small bird, the same as a bird's tweet.

clue.text: Irrational cops suspect plotting

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not right, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Unreasonable police officers suspect a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspect reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiratorial describes people secretly scheming together, so engaged in plotting.

clue.text: Old friend takes doctor home first

indicators.note: a word that takes others into it holds them within its own letters

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
to doctor something is to rig or tamper with it
someone at home is in
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: An old friend brings a doctor home for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is the verb meaning falsify, not a physician, and home is the common crossword stand-in for in.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally means at the beginning or initially, which is what first means as an adverb.

clue.text: Experiment eating cake, assessing body

indicators.note: the word doing the eating swallows the other, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a trial is an experiment or test
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A scientific test in which cake is eaten, while a panel assesses the results.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a panel set up to judge claims or disputes, an adjudicating board.

clue.text: Full theatre allowed more at the back

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
to be let do something is to be allowed to

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its closing letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of more

explanation.surface: A packed theatre lets in more people at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertory or rep theatre is a British company staging a rotating programme of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means well filled or stuffed, especially after eating, so full.

clue.text: Romeo stuffs pocket with obscene bulge

indicators.note: stuffing puts one thing inside another, so the letter goes into the pocket

parts.note: to pot a ball is to pocket it in snooker
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rude means vulgar or obscene

explanation.surface: A lover has something rude bulging in his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Pocket is the snooker verb, to pot a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out from a surface, which is what a bulge does.

clue.text: Lips covered with fake colour of blusher

indicators.note: the first part is covered by the second, which wraps around it

parts.note: a con is a fake or swindle
the lip of a cup is its rim

explanation.surface: Lips coated in fake colour, as with make-up blusher.
explanation.walkthrough: Lips sounds like a mouth but means edges, the rims of vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red, the shade a face turns when blushing hard.

clue.text: Rank actors with second-rate parts

indicators.note: the letter parts the word, splitting it open and sitting in the gap

parts.note: the actors in a production are its cast
B grade is second-rate
and means together with

explanation.surface: A theatre critic grades the actors as second-rate in their roles.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank looks like a grading, picked up by second-rate, but it is a taxi rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab-stand is a place where taxis queue for passengers, called a taxi rank in Britain.

clue.text: Put up with grey blind spoiling sight of NYC

parts.note: to brook something is to tolerate it

indicators.note: spoiling something ruins its form, so the letters are mangled into another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dull grey window blind blocks the view of a New York landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Put up with is the definition-like phrase that actually means tolerate, BROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brooklyn Bridge is a famous suspension bridge over the East River and a tourist attraction in New York City.

clue.text: Yule's beginning before it should, every Christmas?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of Yule
arriving before it should means coming early

explanation.surface: A complaint that Christmas starts too early every year.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that every Christmas is only an example of something recurring annually.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas falls once every twelve months, so something happening each Christmas happens on an annual basis.

clue.text: Poppycock Washington served up, LOL

parts.note: guff is nonsense, like poppycock

indicators.note: in a down entry something served up is lifted from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: Washington dishes out nonsense, and people laugh out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: LOL is text shorthand for laughing out loud, and a guffaw is a loud hearty laugh.

clue.text: Gin's infusion taking ages, you'd say

indicators.note: you'd say points to how the words sound when spoken, not how they are written

parts.note: something taking ages is slow

explanation.surface: Making flavoured gin is a slow process.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloe gin is made by steeping blackthorn berries in gin for months, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloes are the small sour fruit of the blackthorn, steeped in gin to make the liqueur sloe gin.

clue.text: Granny beds camper on island paradise

indicators.note: a word that beds something takes it in, holding it within its own letters

parts.note: nana is a pet name for a grandmother

indicators.note: in an across entry, sitting on something means coming after it, so the island letter is written first

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island
RV, recreational vehicle, is the American term for a camper van

explanation.surface: Grandma puts up a camper on a tropical island paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: On places the camper after the island in this across entry, making IRV, which then sits inside NANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect bliss, and loosely any idyllic place or state of happiness.

clue.text: Excuse me, what's on the bottom of your skirt?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a polite cough to attract attention

definitions.text: what's on the bottom of your skirt?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split into two words: a single turned-up edge of fabric

explanation.surface: Someone politely interrupts to point out something on another person's skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the answer as two words, an article plus the folded edge at the foot of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the throat-clearing sound used to get attention, as excuse me does, and a hem finishes the lower edge of a skirt.

clue.text: After swimming you left with eyes streaming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about loosely and settle in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
U is text speak for you
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: After a swim, someone's eyes are left watering from the chlorine.
explanation.walkthrough: After looks like a time word but is the fodder; swimming is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearful means crying or close to tears, when water streams from the eyes.

clue.text: 50 for one party coming round, put on record

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the following pair is read from right to left

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so for one
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Fifty guests arrive for a party at someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: For one looks like a ratio with 50, but it means for example, abbreviated EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge a complaint or appeal is to file it formally, entering it on the official record.

clue.text: Supply of US arms from Czech handling racket with no trouble

parts.note: Ivan Lendl is the Czech-born tennis champion, wielding a racket
doing something with ease means without trouble

explanation.surface: Weapons supplied from America via a Czech arms racket that goes smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket suggests a criminal scheme, but it is a tennis racket in the hands of Ivan Lendl, eight-time Grand Slam singles champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lend-Lease was the Second World War programme under which the United States supplied weapons and materiel to its allies.
